units.translation: On ⟦1⟧ it should be noted that according to Diodorus XVI, 26, originally virgins prophesied at Delphi; but when one had once been abducted, from then on women over 50 years of age were taken, though still in maiden's dress.
⟦1⟧ penetralia as at 170. 180. ⟦2⟧; with ⟦3⟧ one compares ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧; that woolen fillets are meant is shown by ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧. The ⟦10⟧, of white marble, is also mentioned by ⟦11⟧.
why then did Phoebus cry out from the fillets
the central navel-stone . . clothed with fillets
V. 40 ⟦1⟧ (only here) as murderer; the resolution in the 5th foot is rare, but not unheard of (⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧, Weckl.).

⟦1⟧ see ⟦2⟧ (here 234. 237. 445, and ⟦3⟧ 205, ⟦4⟧ 718; everywhere of the seeking of purification; the sense is different at 176). Here it is connected with ⟦5⟧ (Wieseler), which is why ⟦6⟧ (M) is more elegant than ⟦7⟧ (f g h), which forces everything to be referred to ⟦8⟧. The blood is naturally not that of the mother, but that of the expiatory victim slaughtered by Apollo, V. 282 f.; see the description of the rite ⟦9⟧ (⟦10⟧ [of Jason] ⟦11⟧ [Circe], ⟦12⟧ [of the piglet]). So this has happened recently; Orestes, however, is still waiting for Apollo's reappearance and further instructions. The Pythia, however, can know nothing of this purification, but must think of murder and blood. Also with ⟦13⟧ compare Apoll. V. 694: Jason has seated himself at the hearth ⟦14⟧.
having fixed his great sword in the ground

⟦1⟧ (only here) is naturally said not from visual inspection, but from an obvious inference (see Schütz): this sword must, since the hand still drips, have been drawn recently for murder. The conjecture ⟦2⟧ (Burges) is plausible, but the word is after ⟦3⟧. ⟦4⟧. somewhat tautological, and seems besides to presuppose a purification also of the sword, of which nothing else is known.

⟦1⟧ only here. ⟦2⟧ also has ⟦3⟧ (⟦4⟧, of the golden fleece) and ⟦5⟧; it must have been a rare, sacral word, and for that very reason, as the scholiast also notes, in need of the explanation given in 45 (Weil). Then, however, ⟦6⟧ will refer not to the size of the fillets, but to their significance in the ritual ("mighty").
